exercises.approach: Call rpart with method = "class" and a control that allows splits on 8 rows: minsplit 2, minbucket 1, maxdepth 1, cp 0 and xval 0.
exercises.why: The labels switch from low to high between x = 4 and x = 5, so a single cut there separates them perfectly. x = 2 falls on the low side and x = 7 on the high side.
exercises.wrong: Relying on the default control. rpart's default minsplit is 20, so with only 8 rows it never attempts a split, returns a lone root, and gives x = 2 and x = 7 the same class.

exercises.approach: Request type = "prob", read its column names, and select columns by name rather than by position.
exercises.why: The fixture sets levels = c("low", "high"), so the columns appear in that order. Each leaf is pure, so the rows for x = 2 and x = 7 are (1, 0) and (0, 1) and each sums to 1.
exercises.wrong: Taking `prob[, 2]` as the probability of high. In the pruning example the factor is built without explicit levels, so they sort alphabetically to high, low, and column 2 would be low.
exercises.verify: `identical(colnames(prob), c("low", "high"))` returns TRUE and `max(abs(rowSums(prob) - 1))` returns a value below 1e-12.

exercises.approach: Store the result of prune(fit, cp = 1) in a new object and count leaves in that object's frame.
exercises.why: The single split takes misclassifications from 4 of 8 to 0, a relative improvement of 1, and pruning at that complexity removes it. The frame keeps only the root, which is itself the one leaf.
exercises.wrong: Counting leaves on fit after calling prune. prune returns a new tree and leaves fit unchanged, so that count still shows 2.

exercises.approach: Report training accuracy as a fit statistic, and choose depth or cp on development folds before a separate final assessment.
exercises.why: One cut already classifies all 8 training rows correctly. Any deeper tree would also score 8 of 8, so training accuracy cannot rank the candidates at all.
exercises.wrong: Selecting the deepest tree because it is also perfect on training data. With noisy labels, extra splits would isolate single rows, and only rows outside training show whether those splits help.
exercises.verify: `all(as.character(predict(fit, d, type = "class")) == as.character(d$label))` returns TRUE, which shows fit on the 8 training rows only.

exercises.approach: Wrap predict in a function that stops on any NA or non-finite x before rpart sees it.
exercises.why: This application declares that it scores only complete finite inputs. The check sits in the wrapper, so the rule is visible in code and does not depend on how rpart routes missing values internally.
exercises.wrong: Passing NA straight to predict. rpart has its own rules for missing predictors and still returns a class, so a row with no x value gets a confident looking label and nothing is logged.

exercises.approach: Score x = 1000 through the wrapper and report it as a value far outside the training range 1 to 8.
exercises.why: Every x above the cut lands in the high leaf, so 1000 gets exactly the same class and probabilities as x = 5. A tree's leaves are constant regions, so there is no trend to extend.
exercises.wrong: Reading the result as stronger evidence for high because 1000 is far beyond the cut. The tree gives x = 5 and x = 1000 an identical output, and no training row says anything about values that large.
